passage:
A kindergarten held classes outdoors once a week. Children counted leaves, listened for birds, built shapes with sticks, and watched insects.
Some parents worried the children would get dirty or distracted. Teachers explained that outdoor learning still had goals: observation, language, movement, and cooperation.
After several weeks, parents noticed their children asking more questions about weather and plants.
The forest did not replace the classroom. It expanded it.
Children learned that knowledge is not only printed on paper or shown on screens. Some lessons crawl, fall, grow, and fly. A living classroom changes every time students enter it.
